title: Slow Down to Hear God Again
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this.
script: You haven’t lost God; you’ve lost quiet. Hurry turns His whisper into static. Jesus slipped away early to pray, alone (Mark 1:35). Try a three-day noise fast: first and last 15 minutes, no phone, no music. Stand by a window or step outside. Breathe, Be still … and know. Read Psalm 46:10 once. Then say, Speak, Lord, your servant is listening, and wait two minutes. Jot what comes—scripture, a nudge, a name to encourage. Do it again tomorrow. He’s not hiding; we’re hurrying. Slow down, and you’ll remember what His voice sounds like.

title: Stop Striving, Start Receiving
hook: You might be trying too hard—here’s how to receive.
script: When prayer feels like pushing a boulder, switch from striving to attending. God’s voice is more like a breath than a shout. Try this simple lectio divina. Take Psalm 46:10. Read it slowly. Notice the one word that warms or stings. Tell God why that word matters right now. Then rest in silence for sixty seconds as if sunbathing in His presence. If thoughts wander, gently return to that word. Repeat three times this week. Clarity often comes not as fireworks, but as a steady light. Keep it simple. Receive.

title: Clear the Clutter, Hear the Whisper
hook: If shame and mental clutter are loud, listen to this.
script: Sometimes we can’t hear God because unprocessed guilt buzzes like a neon sign. Pray Psalm 139:23–24: Search me, God… Then be specific: I’m carrying this. Confess it, not to grovel, but to agree with truth. Now receive grace. Say, Because of Jesus, I am forgiven and clean. Finally, replace the noise with truth—Be still and know that I am God. For a weekly reset, start a Sabbath window: three unhurried hours, no tasks, no scrolling. Walk, rest, and be with Him. Quiet makes room for a whisper. His mercy turns up the volume.
